title: CurbCut findings
description: Merged review of one pull request, written by the cc-review mode. Every finding has an evidence tier. A proven finding must cite at least one fact_id that exists in facts.json; a flagged finding is a reviewer's judgment and must say why in one sentence. Out-of-reach checks are always listed. Facts that could not be interpreted go to not_scanned with a reason; nothing is silently dropped. The counts in summary must equal the lengths of the lists. No em dashes in any text.

pr_id.description: Report id, for example pr-1 or pr-1-run2.

facts_file.description: Repository-relative path to the facts.json this review used.

generated_by.description: Mode or tool that wrote this file, for example cc-review.

findings.description: Proven and flagged findings, one per (sc, page, selector) after deduplication.

out_of_reach.description: Checks this method cannot perform for the changed pages, such as caption accuracy or real screen reader experience.

not_scanned.description: Facts or pages that could not be turned into a finding, with the reason.

sc.description: WCAG 2.2 success criterion number, for example 1.4.3.

id.description: F001, F002 and so on, unique in this file.

severity.description: Orders the list. Never removes a finding.

page.description: Page path relative to codes/fixture/src, for example quiz-signup.html.

selector.description: CSS selector of the element, as in facts.json when a fact exists.

fact_ids.description: Required and non-empty for proven. May be empty for flagged.

reason.description: One sentence: what was measured (proven) or why the reviewer believes it (flagged).

who_is_affected.description: Plain language: who is affected and how.

fixable.description: True when a code change in the fixture can resolve it.

source.description: engine, or the Explore subagent that raised it.
